economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00052227492: Two-pass public-evidence and corrective gap-closure audit for Flexential's Minneapolis-Chaska data center on parcel 30.0590020 at 3500 Lyman Boulevard. The review covered Carver County parcel, valuation-notice, tax-statement and payment records; City of Chaska permit, inspection, agenda, archive, budget, utility and annual-financial-report sources; Minnesota DEED, Revenue, statutory, environmental, workforce and utility-regulatory sources; federal environmental, workplace-safety and county-economic access points; current and archived operator, predecessor, career and ESG materials; contractor and supplier references; and education, workforce and recipient-reported community sources for 2013-2026. Twenty-three quantitative observations are preserved: a source-projected original investment lower bound; three later non-cumulative permit values; current floor area and critical-load UPS capacity; three annual parcel-tax payments; one current parcel-tax bill; five exact-parcel taxable-market-value stocks for payable 2023-2027; and eight historical Via West Inc. estimated-actual-value observations. The exact parcel statements crosswalk the 2023-2025 city-table values to parcel 30.0590020, but the duplicate value concepts are alternative assessor presentations and are not additive. Stream's facilities at 1706 and 1708 West Creek Lane, the IP Stream Minneapolis LLC development agreement and its municipal rebates are outside the selected 3500 Lyman Boulevard project boundary and are not duplicated in this fragment; the six base Stream rebate rows require reassignment or removal from this target by the orchestrator because project fragments are append-only. Permit values are administrative estimates and are not summed because scopes may overlap. Parcel taxes span all taxing jurisdictions and special assessments, not City-only receipts or net benefit. No synthesis fragment is added because candidate-by-candidate review found no defensible project inputs for construction labor, realized operating employment or payroll, supplier payments, metered energy or water, emissions, facility-specific incentive value, public-service costs, quantified community transfers, or a causal county employment, wage or GDP effect. prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Corrective public-evidence and candidate-modeling audit for Switch Las Vegas NAP7, the individual real-property parcel and original SUPERNAP building at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard. The review covered Clark County assessor and ownership history, Treasurer, Accela permits, rights-of-way, planning, air quality, budgets and financial reports; Nevada incentive, tax and utility-regulatory sources; operator, SEC, workforce, supplier and contractor materials; and recipient-reported community records for 2005-2026. Six direct observations remain after the corrective pass; no wider Core Campus capital expenditure, combined incentive audit, later facility, personal property, tenant equipment, vendor equipment, company-wide employment or parcel-transfer price is recast as NAP7 contribution. One modeled synthesis is retained under the last-resort modeling gate: the fiscal-year 2027 real-property bill defines an exactly same-account assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even threshold. It is not actual public cost, collected revenue, jurisdictional receipt or a net fiscal result. Candidate models for investment, construction, suppliers, operations, resources, community benefits, net fiscal effects and county employment, GDP and wages were rejected for missing facility inputs, incompatible scope or timing, overlap, non-identification or lack of decision relevance. NAP7 employment, payroll, local supplier payments, metered electricity and water, personal-property tax, realized abatement, jurisdictional receipts, actual project-attributable public costs and net fiscal impact remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00214321737: Corrective public-evidence and model-eligibility audit for Markley Group's Lowell data center at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way in Lowell, Middlesex County. The selected IM3 footprint is one building inside a three-building assessor parcel, so every sourced amount remains at campus or company/county scope and is unallocated to the selected building. modeled_scope_note: Foundational accounts re-audited under study-modeling-policy 1.3.0 after renewed direct-evidence searches. Apple Mesa retains three narrowly scoped business-personal-property FTZ counterfactuals from its project fragment; Switch Citadel retains four exact fiscal arithmetic or break-even syntheses; Digital Crossroad Hammond retains two two-account paid-tax arithmetic or break-even syntheses from its project fragment. All other legacy foundational estimates were removed because direct inputs, project scope, time profiles, local allocation, causal identification, or decision relevance were not defensible. Reported observations, forecasts, and remaining models stay separate. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Last-resort NAP7 modeling pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact, same-property-account fiscal-year 2027 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed property-tax bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, resource, community and county outcome candidates were rejected because compatible NAP7 inputs or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00214321737: Last-resort Markley Lowell model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact same-account FY2026 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed four-quarter real-property bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, fiscal-net, resource, community and each GDP, employment and wage candidate are rejected separately in the evidence fragment because compatible inputs, scope alignment, non-overlap proof or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00300974499: Corrective policy-1.3.0 synthesis. Three legacy combined real-and-personal-property FTZ counterfactuals are superseded by narrower business-personal-property-only estimates because the Apple BPP account directly exhibits the 5% assessment ratio while the real-property account has a different valuation base. The replacements hold observed effective tax rates and full cash value constant and isolate only the assessment-ratio component; they are not cash grants, audited forgone-revenue amounts or net fiscal benefits. All other legacy Apple Mesa estimates fail the direct-evidence, scope, time-profile, geography or decision-relevance gates and are marked for removal in the evidence fragment. prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00388148510: Project-scoped modeled synthesis for TierPoint Little Rock. Eleven resolved-year real-property taxable values are multiplied by signed code 03/33 school, city, and county millage components; 2025 is excluded because its observed Amount Due does not disclose the underlying revised taxable value. A conditional zero-leave FTE-equivalent floor translates the facility-specific 2012 onsite NOC staffed 24/7/365 statement without claiming employee headcount or payroll. Two low-confidence engineering sensitivities use one, not both, of the redundant 3,000 kVA utility transformers and expose hypothetical power-factor, utilization, and PUE assumptions. Every estimate is modeled_not_observed_or_audited and excluded from sourced-record counts, cash receipts, realized-benefit totals, and net-fiscal claims. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00598261190: Dedicated last-resort model-eligibility pass for State Farm Olathe under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Four bounded syntheses are retained: the exact 2025 parcel-tax-payment identity as a same-account public-service-cost break-even threshold, plus low-confidence descriptive 2024 Johnson County GDP, employment and wage comparison gaps using the repository's pre-2016 inverse-distance benchmark. No estimate is an observed cost, net fiscal result or causal facility effect. Supplier/local-spend and community-allocation candidates, an HPIP credit counterfactual, and causal county designs are rejected because the project-specific inputs, scope matches, non-overlap proof or identification conditions recorded in the evidence fragment are absent. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00838817907: Corrective metric-specific synthesis for TierPoint Charlotte Center Park (CL4). Two independent staffing-equivalent sensitivities translate facility-specific continuous NOC and security coverage statements into the FTE capacity needed to cover one simultaneous post; neither is an observed employee count, the functions are not summed, and employer, overlap, shift, absence, residence and payroll remain unknown. A separate opening-configuration electricity sensitivity annualizes the directly reported 1.215 MW usable UPS capacity across utilization and PUE scenarios while checking the source-reported 3,000 kVA service capacity under power-factor assumptions. It is a theoretical nameplate envelope, not metered use, a true-value bound or an economic contribution. No model is created from 530 tons of cooling because electrical demand would require unobserved COP, part-load, redundancy and operating-hour inputs, and no model is created from generator counts, unit ratings, runtime or fuel storage because emergency standby nameplates do not measure annual operation. prj_study_im3_building_00844389014: Second-pass model review retains one bounded resource identity only. It reproduces Google-reported 2024 Montgomery County water consumption as withdrawal minus discharge after converting displayed million-gallon values to gallons, with a rounding envelope. Direct searches of Clarksville utility/public-works pages, county stormwater records, TDEC/EPA portals and CDE/TVA materials did not surface a building meter, utility bill or a compatible canonical observed-water metric. The amount remains unallocated across the location and inventory buildings; discharge may be engineering-estimated. No transferred multiplier, supplier-retention assumption, energy proxy, fiscal result, public-cost threshold, payroll estimate or causal county outcome is modeled. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Residual synthesis after the SV1 public-source audit. It retains one exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold and three reproducible but low-confidence county comparison gaps. The county gaps use 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and an inverse-distance-weighted 20-county benchmark; very wide fit envelopes are retained because Santa Clara County matches poorly. No model converts capacity to consumption, permit value to jobs, or unidentified vendor and community activity to local benefits. prj_study_im3_building_00978934687: Corrective residual synthesis for Digital Crossroad DX-1 under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Of 43 legacy estimates, none is retained unchanged: 41 are directed for removal and two are revised using the complete 2024-pay-2025 paid-tax base for the leasehold real account and DX Hammond JV LLC personal-property account. The revised contribution is an exact account-level aggregation across local taxing authorities, and the companion public-service-cost estimate is only the equal-cost break-even identity; neither is an audited recipient receipt, observed public cost or net fiscal result. New estimate IDs prevent silent mutation of the legacy base and their notes identify the superseded estimates for orchestrator reconciliation. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution. prj_study_im3_building_01132541700: Four bounded syntheses are retained after direct-record search: one deterministic conversion of Meta's rounded 2024 Henrico water-withdrawal observation and three governed, descriptive county comparison gaps. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. Every retained estimate is visibly modeled, unallocated to the selected building, non-additive, and noncausal. prj_study_im3_campus_00019988712: Residual synthesis after the Meta Prineville direct-evidence audit. One medium-confidence unit conversion carries Meta's rounded 2024 facility-level water-withdrawal observation from megaliters to gallons because the shared direct register has no compatible annual-withdrawal metric. The three low-confidence county benchmark comparisons were removed: even with fit-sensitivity envelopes and explicit non-causal labels, they do not materially improve decisions about this campus and remain vulnerable to concurrent Meta expansions, Apple's separate campus and unrelated county changes. No supplier, construction, payroll, household-spending, tax-abatement, public-service-cost or fiscal-net model is retained because local inputs and same-scope evidence are insufficient. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Residual synthesis after the Google The Dalles public-source audit. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps are retained because the direct record does not identify causal county outcomes. Each benchmark uses the available 2001-2005 pre-opening history, excludes all study counties from a 20-county inverse-distance-weighted donor pool, and carries a fit-sensitivity envelope. No model converts broad investment or permit values to jobs, onsite contractor counts to supplier output, utility-system loads to campus consumption, tax bills to payments, or unmatched incentive formulas and public costs to a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_campus_00675108684: Dedicated last-resort Boydton model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Retained syntheses are limited to exact arithmetic over cited compatible observations: a five-fiscal-year average of the operator-reported portfolio property-tax total, its explicitly conditional same-scope public-cost break-even identity, and annual sums of identified LVL/Herbert Fund 301 components. All remain unallocated, modeled rather than observed, and non-additive to their source totals. COF phase investment, operating headcount, construction, resources, suppliers, induced effects, causal comparisons and net fiscal impact were rejected because overlap, timing, scope or required project inputs remain unresolved.

project_description: Expedient MKE1 is a colocation data center operated by Expedient at 4777 W Ironwood Drive in Franklin, Milwaukee County, Wisconsin. This project account covers the single adaptive-reuse facility and its parcel, not Expedient's wider regional portfolio, and keeps the October 2021 opening snapshot separate from later current specifications. Public records trace the pre-existing building, leased operation, 2022 ownership transfer, and subsequent facility permits.
